justification: A learned policy decides when the agent must defer to a human expert rather than proceed unaided; "extensive experiments in Minecraft" are lab trials of a new framework, not deployed practice.
Object of study is intrinsic self-correction and the form of its reflection feedback (constrained vs free-text), an audit of one named revision mechanism run in the lab on Qwen3-8B.

Concludes recursive refinement (self-criticism, stress-testing, integrating feedback) is the effective architectural feature; tested by comparing a linear against a refinement-layer pipeline over nine lab cases.
CR-Planner "iteratively select[s] and execut[es] sub-goals", with a sub-goal critic choosing the next step; validated on competitive programming, math and retrieval benchmarks in the lab.
Contribution is the Adaptive Iterative Refinement strategy that self-corrects errors across passes; evidence is lab benchmark accuracy on VCR, A-OKVQA and DailyLife-MRC for a newly built framework.
IoT's inner-dialogue loop regenerates a response from generated critique prompts, i.e. autonomous response refinement; validated on GPQA, Game of 24, Mini Crosswords and HotpotQA in the lab.

"Ablation studies identify iterative verification as the primary contributor", so the verifier's constraint check carries the claim; evidence is accuracy on the authors' own PRIME-Bench, a lab evaluation.
The generator is progressively rewritten from a VLM critic's feedback in the loop; claim rests on lab benchmark gains (ConceptMix, T2I-CompBench, Visual Jenga) for a proposed test-time strategy.
IdealGPT "iteratively decomposes" a question into sub-questions that determine the next step until confidence is reached; validated zero-shot on VCR and SNLI-VE in the lab.

Audits whether iterative LLM refinement helps at all, finding a 37.6% rise in critical vulnerabilities over rounds; evidence is a lab controlled experiment (400 samples, 40 rounds, four prompting strategies).
Novelty is the ILP-learned rule table acting as an online step-level verifier that diagnoses violations; validated on the CLUTRR benchmark over five models, a lab study of a new technique.
Adaptive-Consistency keeps the sampling scheme intact and only varies how many samples are drawn via a stopping criterion; validated across 17 reasoning and code datasets with three LLMs.
CRAFT's novelty is turning the prompt into explicit dependency-structured constraints that a VLM verifies, updating only on violation; lab benchmark gains across model families, no deployed use.
Formalises composed LM calls as probabilistic programs whose control flow and dynamic structure fix the order of steps; it is a conceptual reframing of existing techniques with no evaluation.
Contribution is a small LM trained to act as a verifier module issuing fine-grained corrective instructions, i.e. the judgement itself; validated on three graph-based datasets in the lab.

The agent perceives its own rendered output and iterates on the result to meet the objective, a revise-on-visual-feedback loop; offered as a design framework with usage scenarios and proof-of-concept agents only.
GenPRM is a process reward model that reasons and runs code verification before judging each step, i.e. the acceptance judgement; validated on ProcessBench and math benchmarks in the lab.
T1 is a two-stage verification pipeline that filters candidates with tools before small-LM judgement, contributing how the check is produced; validated on the MATH benchmark, lab only.
CGR probes answer certainty to terminate reasoning early against a token budget, an adaptive halting rule; validated on AIME2025 across 64 seeds in the lab.

Negative early exit halts unproductive trajectories and adaptive boosting reallocates reclaimed compute, targeting latency rather than search shape; evaluated by varying these mechanisms inside vLLM in the lab.
DCR's primitive generates multiple candidate solutions then reconciles them, amplifying correct minority reports, i.e. exploration and selection; validated on AIME 2024/2025 in the lab.
The contribution is a compute-optimal strategy that allocates test-time compute adaptively per prompt by difficulty; evidence is a lab FLOPs-matched comparison against best-of-N and a larger model.
TAB is a learned policy allocating per-turn token budgets under a global constraint; validated on diverse agentic benchmarks in the lab, with no deployment or real users reported.
Studies a verification-cost-limited setting and allocates verifier calls where most informative, spending rather than reshaping search; validated on MATH with 44% fewer verifier calls, lab only.

Claim is that verifier-based guidance is essential and verifier-free trace cloning is suboptimal, so the check carries the paper; a proof plus lab corroboration on didactic and math problems at 3/8/32B.
